input.quote: (i) Sanofi may, without consent of RevMed, assign this Agreement or its rights and obligations hereunder in whole or in part to any Affiliate of Sanofi, and RevMed may, with the consent of Sanofi (not to be unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned), assign this Agreement or its rights and obligations hereunder in whole or in part to any Affiliate of RevMed; and
input.rationale: Section 15.2 meets the preferred position. We may assign to any Sanofi Affiliate without RevMed's consent (p0610) and, without consent, to a successor in a merger, acquisition or similar transaction or a sale of all or substantially all related assets (p0611), giving us the affiliate and M&A carve-out we require. RevMed must obtain our consent (not to be unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned) for affiliate assignments and cannot transfer the RevMed Licensed Patents to a Third Party without our consent (p0615). RevMed's reciprocal right to assign to a Change of Control successor without consent sits at the fallback level and is mitigated by the Acquiror Family firewall conditions in p0613-p0614 (acquired party remains a wholly-owned subsidiary, IP and R&D assets stay with the Acquired Party Family, separation from Acquiror competing programs, no Know-How exchange) and by our own option to terminate on a RevMed Change of Control under Section 12.2(a)(ii) (p0489). Critically, no RevMed termination or re-pricing right is triggered by a Sanofi change of control; RevMed's termination rights run only to material breach, insolvency, competing product and cessation. Noted but not flagged: the Section 9.7(a) tax gross-up where withholding arises from a Sanofi assignment to an Affiliate, and the cessation of post-termination royalties payable to us on a Change of Control of Sanofi (p0508), are narrow economic consequences rather than vendor exit or re-pricing rights.
